Add a search box over the layer's own features

Source: R/add_feature_search.R
add_feature_search.Rd

Adds a search box that suggests features of a layer as you type, matching a column such as a name. Choosing a suggestion moves the map to the feature and outlines it. Matching ignores case and accents, so "cordoba" finds "Córdoba". Unlike mapgl::add_geocoder_control(), which searches places around the world, this searches your data.

Usage

add_feature_search(
  map,
  layer_id,
  search_column,
  detail_column = NULL,
  placeholder = NULL,
  max_results = 8,
  locale = "en-US",
  position = "top-right",
  width = 240,
  highlight_color = "#1f2328",
  labels = context_labels()
)

Arguments

map

A map created with mapgl::maplibre() or mapgl::mapboxgl().

layer_id

ID of the layer to search. Its source must be an sf object or inline GeoJSON added in R.

search_column

Column to search, such as the feature names.

detail_column

Optional column shown next to each suggestion to tell apart features with the same name, such as the province.

placeholder

Text shown in the empty search box. NULL (the default) uses the search_placeholder label, "Search…".

max_results

Maximum number of suggestions.

locale

Locale used to sort the suggestions alphabetically.

position

Corner for the search box: one of "top-left", "top-right", "bottom-left" or "bottom-right".

width

Width of the search box in pixels.

highlight_color

Color of the outline drawn around the chosen feature.

labels

Panel texts, as returned by context_labels().

Value

The modified map object.

Details

The search box works with the keyboard: arrow keys move through the suggestions, Enter chooses one and Escape closes them.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(mapgl)

maplibre(center = c(-64, -38.5), zoom = 3.4) |>
  add_fill_layer(id = "deptos", source = ar_departments, fill_color = "#9ecae1") |>
  add_feature_search(
    layer_id = "deptos",
    search_column = "department",
    detail_column = "province"
  )
} # }
